source.title: Causes and Consequences of Representational Similarity in Machine Learning Models
source.authors: Ze-Yu Li; Hung Anh Vu; Damilola Awofisayo; Emily Wenger

record.tranche_reason: The study experimentally tests whether training-data and task overlap affect representation similarity, and identifies overlap as a cause that can account for similarity otherwise attributed to broader convergence.
record.gate_note: The study varies dataset and task overlap and measures representation similarity, so these results are included. Transfer attack success rates are downstream outcomes, not direct measurements of the claim versions' representational convergence, and are not recorded as rows. Accuracy, FID, generated samples, and results cited from prior work are also excluded.
record.test_reason: The study varies shared training data and shared tasks in pairs of same-architecture models and measures CKA. This bears directly on V7's claim that shared data or objectives, not a common model of reality, explain alignment. Its appendix plots seven similarity metrics for every setting, which bears on V6's metric dependence. It does not vary scale, modality pairing, mapping or features, so V1–V5 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that dataset overlap and task overlap each increase representational similarity, and that combining them gives the strongest effect, measured by mutual information. They attribute the flat Llama dataset-overlap result to LoRA finetuning. They report that greater similarity coincides with higher transfer of adversarial examples, though jailbreak transfer between Llama pairs stayed high and flat.
record.recipe_differences: This is a controlled overlap study measuring CKA and other similarity metrics, not a reproduction of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis or the original convergent-learning method. It manipulates data and task overlap rather than model scale.
record.method_sensitivity: The Llama dataset-overlap results show little or no trend, whereas image-model results generally trend upward. The study also evaluates seven similarity metrics, but does not describe metric-specific differences in the text; most such comparisons appear in appendix figures.

fits_no_version.finding: Higher data/task overlap increases transfer adversarial-attack success between ViT/ResNet pairs. Jailbreak transfer between Llama pairs stays flat and high.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representational similarity induced by training overlap raises adversarial transferability between models.

record.problems: The study primarily uses CKA, whose alignment scores the authors say are difficult to interpret and lack an established threshold for strong alignment. Model sizes are limited, production-scale effects are not tested, and only same-architecture pairs are compared. Llama results are exceptions to the dataset-overlap trend. Many detailed similarity-metric outcomes are presented only in figures.
record.rows_left_out: Not all metric-comparison plots in Appendix A.2 were extracted; the sampled ResNet18 comparisons in Figure 9 are included, but corresponding plots for other models and datasets were omitted. Transfer-attack results in §6 and Appendix A.3-A.4 were excluded because they report downstream attack behavior rather than direct representation-similarity measurements.

untested.parts: Similarity across model scale or capability is not compared, and only same-architecture pairs are used.
Pairs differ by data or task, not only by initialization. Attack pairs share seeds, and pretrained models share an initialization.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation tests.
No feature or circuit universality analysis.
Input distribution and out-of-distribution dependence are not tested; only in-distribution validation sets are used.

Not tested: whether alignment plateaus or stays incomplete at scale, whether overlap explains similarity across different architectures or in production-scale models, and any test against a common-model-of-reality account.

missing.what: Per-metric regression slopes and R² for all seven metrics, showing the overlap trend is metric-dependent (e.g. SVCCA R²≈0.00–0.20 for ViTs vs CKA R²>0.9)
nanoGPT (Shakespeare, TinyStories, task splitting) and diffusion UNet results across metrics
CIFAR-100 finetuned ResNet/ViT dataset and task splitting CKA fits
Mutual information between overlap and CKA by overlap type: 0.584 (dataset), 0.771 (task), 0.891 (both)

record.verdict_notes: Key confound: the ResNet/ViT and Llama pairs are finetuned from the same pretrained checkpoint. The high similarity at zero overlap may therefore be inherited, not convergent. The zero-overlap ViT CKA intercepts rise roughly with size (0.55, 0.62, 0.71, 0.68), but the authors do not analyze scale, so this is not a V1 test. The reader's rows mislabel every operation as 'scaling' and call readable regression values 'figure only'.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether representational alignment rises as models get larger or more capable.
Does not measure alignment between paired images and captions or compare vision and language models.
Uses training seeds in experiments but does not test whether different initializations learn shared features or subspaces.
Does not test mapping, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired representation interchange.
Does not identify recurring interpretable features or circuits.
Does not test input-distribution or out-of-distribution dependence. It reports multiple similarity measures in appendix figures, but does not give their plotted values in text.
Tests controlled overlap in the study's settings, not whether training overlap explains similarity in production-scale models or across different architectures.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Varied dataset overlap between paired models and measured CKA.
rows.note: The text describes CKA as steadily rising with overlap; the plotted regression value cannot be assigned confidently from the flattened figure text.
rows.check: The operation is mislabelled 'scaling'; it is a dataset-overlap manipulation. Values are readable, not figure-only. Fig 4(a)/Fig 17 CKA fits are: ResNet18 y=0.02x+0.95 (R²=0.99); ResNet50 y=0.03x+0.91 (0.99); ResNet101 y=0.02x+0.91 (0.24); ResNet152 y=0.03x+0.89 (0.99). ViT tiny/small/base/large are y=0.03x+0.55 (0.91), 0.04x+0.62 (0.98), 0.03x+0.71 (0.97), 0.04x+0.68 (0.96). The effect is consistent but small: +0.02–0.04 CKA from disjoint to identical data, on a baseline of 0.55–0.95 at zero overlap. Models are all finetuned from the same timm pretrained weights, a shared-initialization confound. Partial relative to 'shared data explains alignment'. ResNet101 R² is only 0.24.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Varied dataset overlap between paired models and measured CKA.
rows.value: No meaningful trend reported; figure regression R2=0.01, y=0.02x+0.91.
rows.note: The authors describe lack of trend in the Llama results; regression assignment follows the figure's model labels.
rows.check: The value is misassigned: 'y=0.02x+0.91' is ResNet101's fit, not Llama-1B's. Fig 4(b)/Fig 19(b) Llama CKA fits are all about y=-0.00x+1.00 with R²=0.01–0.03, and CKA is about 0.999 at every overlap. The per-model assignment of R² is uncertain in the flattened text.

source_check.correct: Llama dataset-overlap CKA fits are y=-0.00x+1.00, with R² spanning 0.01–0.03 and CKA approximately 0.999. The fit y=0.02x+0.91 belongs to ResNet101 and has R²=0.24.
source_check.problem: The reported regression equation belongs to ResNet101, not Llama-1B.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct

rows.value: No meaningful trend reported; figure regression R2=0.02, y=-0.00x+1.00.

rows.check: CKA is about 0.999 at all overlaps (slope -0.00, R² 0.01–0.03). Representations are essentially identical because of LoRA on a shared base, so the measure has almost no room to move. The operation is mislabelled 'scaling'.

source_check.correct: The flat equation and negligible overlap effect are supported; the flattened text does not securely associate R²=0.02 with Llama-3B.
source_check.problem: Individual Llama R² assignments cannot be verified from the flattened figure layout.

rows.subject: ViT/tiny
rows.operation_detail: Varied task overlap while keeping the images and dataset overlap constant; measured CKA.
rows.note: The text says increasing task overlap positively correlates with CKA when data points are identical.
rows.check: The stage is probably wrong: Table 5 lists ColorShapeDigit800K results under 'finetuned image classification models', and only ResNet18 is stated as trained from scratch. The operation is mislabelled 'scaling'. Values are readable from Fig 6: slopes 0.19–0.43 CKA per overlap level (R² 0.65–0.88). CKA rises from near 0–0.2 at level 1 to about 0.5–0.75 at level 3, a large effect with the data held fixed.

source_check.correct: ViT/tiny is finetuned from pretrained weights in the main image-classifier experiments.
source_check.problem: The training stage is incorrectly recorded as trained from scratch.
